title: Gold, Grey, or Neither: The Moon Through the Telescope

content.question: Is the moon actually gold, as I read, or is it grey like the stones I have been sitting beside all week?
content.method: At dusk, after my afternoon of pretending not to care, I climbed onto the telescope and sat there until the moon rose clear of the western rocks. I looked for a long time, switching my attention between the moon and the grey standing stone so I could compare them without trusting my memory, which is a poor witness. I counted the colours I could honestly name and ignored the ones I wanted to see.
content.result: The moon was not gold. It was the pale grey of old clay that has been left out in the rain, with a faint warm edge near the bottom that might have been gold or might have been me wanting it. The standing stone was darker and cooler. I am keeping the word gold out of the record until a second evening agrees with me, and I am not going to say so twice.
